newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to ban smoking at most federal offices.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to ban smoking at most federal offices.

text.p: President Bill Clinton intends to issue an executive order this week banning smoking in most U.S. federal government offices, senior administration officials said on Tuesday.

"The final language has not been nailed down, but it will happen this week," one official said of the directive, which would apply to all government buildings, except those used by Congress and the federal courts.
"Currently every federal agency sets its own rules," the official said. "The president will set a standard for all the executive branch."

The U.S. military and many federal agencies already restrict smoking in their facilities. The presidential order would ban smoking in virtually every building owned or leased by the federal government.
One administration official said the ban was expected to apply to smoking in courtyards and near the entrances of federal buildings as well.

White House officials also said that they expected an internal review of the tobacco settlement between the states and the industry to be completed by mid-August but that Clinton would not issue his assessment until September.

Under the settlement plan, the tobacco industry would pay out $368 billion over 25 years to settle 40 state lawsuits. The industry would have to make marketing and advertising concessions and agree to tough health warning labels, but in exchange it would get immunity from class action lawsuits in the future.
Clinton has already said he would like to modify the accord to ensure that the Federal Drug Administration has unquestioned control over the regulation of nicotine.
